title: Cognitive Load Analysis in the Draft
description: AIL 606 textbook section connecting cognitive load analysis in the draft to cognitive load diagnosis table with intrinsic/extraneous/germane load evidence, reader notes, support moments, and revision evidence.
learning_objectives: Classify a screen's demand into intrinsic, extraneous, and germane load with evidence.
Attribute each load source to a specific feature, not a vague overall feeling.
Prescribe the type-appropriate move (segment, remove, protect) for each source.
Recognize when a "reduce load" suggestion would actually cut germane processing.
